websites.title: Websites
websites.summary: Expand the web vocabulary with standalone subjects for privacy, accessibility, discovery, publishing, performance, archives, and infrastructure. Explore proposed drawings alongside reusable references.
websites.principle: One subject. One clear meaning. Many useful aliases.

entries.name: Hardware security token
entries.meaning: A physical key for signing in.
entries.brief: One compact USB security token: short body, integrated circular touch contact, and exposed USB connector. No padlock or key overlay.
entries.why: Adds a distinct physical authentication object beyond a generic key.

entries.name: Webcam privacy cover
entries.meaning: A physical shutter that blocks a webcam.
entries.brief: One small sliding webcam cover shown partly open: an elongated adhesive base, a circular lens opening, and its integrated sliding shutter. Keep the cover freestanding; omit the computer, camera, eye symbol, and lock.
entries.why: A tangible privacy control beyond locks and shields. Existing webcam subjects do not replace a drawing of the separate cover.

entries.name: Trackball
entries.meaning: A pointing device operated by rolling a stationary ball.
entries.brief: One freestanding trackball viewed from above at a slight angle: a large exposed ball seated in a low ergonomic base, with two integrated buttons. Keep the ball dominant and omit the hand, cursor, and computer.
entries.why: Adds a distinct input device with a recognizable ball-and-base silhouette; useful for accessible web interaction without implying it suits every user.

entries.name: Braille display
entries.meaning: A tactile device for reading digital content.
entries.brief: One slim refreshable Braille display seen from above, with a row of integrated tactile cells along its top and two broad navigation keys below. Use a few grouped raised dots as physical pin texture; omit readable text, a screen, hands, or a separate accessibility symbol.
entries.why: Represents tactile access through the device itself. Existing Braille books and dot symbols are related subjects, not this piece of hardware. The physical pin details need a small-size legibility check.

entries.name: Foot pedal switch
entries.meaning: An input switch operated with a foot.
entries.brief: One low wedge-shaped foot pedal with an integrated hinged top, broad ribbed tread, and a short cable emerging from its rear. Omit the foot, computer, arrows, and extra pedals.
entries.why: Broadens input beyond keyboards and pointers with one complete physical control. Do not present it as a universal accessibility solution.

entries.name: Tally counter
entries.meaning: A handheld counting device; a metaphor for visits and events.
entries.brief: One mechanical tally counter with a rounded case, a narrow inset counter window, a top thumb plunger, and a small side reset knob. Leave the window blank; omit digits, a hand, charts, and badges.
entries.why: Exploratory metaphor: connects web measurement to a single counting object. It adds counting to the existing speed and time vocabulary. The plunger must remain clear without relying on numbers.

entries.name: Printing press
entries.meaning: A physical publishing tool for a website’s publishing vocabulary.
entries.brief: One compact tabletop screw printing press in front view: a rigid upright frame, an integrated central screw with a short crossbar handle, and a flat platen above the base. Omit paper, lettering, ink drops, and a person.
entries.why: Exploratory publishing metaphor. This is a complete mechanical tool, not an empty frame for another icon; the screw and platen are essential to recognition.

entries.name: Backup tape cartridge
entries.meaning: A removable tape cartridge for stored backups.
entries.brief: One square backup tape cartridge with a clipped corner, an integrated recessed circular hub, and a small shutter detail along one edge. Use an unmarked casing; omit labels, letters, a drive, arrows, and a cloud.
entries.why: A direct storage object for website operations. Its cartridge shape should stay distinct from a cassette, floppy disk, and generic document.

entries.name: USB Ethernet adapter
entries.meaning: An adapter that provides a wired network connection.
entries.brief: One USB Ethernet adapter as a complete connected object: a compact rectangular body with an integral Ethernet socket, a short attached cable, and a USB plug at its end. Omit the laptop, loose network cable, arrows, and logos.
entries.why: A directly useful connectivity subject. The adapter and permanently attached lead form one natural object rather than a combination of separate icons.

entries.name: Network switch
entries.meaning: A device that connects wired network equipment.
entries.brief: One low rectangular network switch with an integrated row of Ethernet ports and two indicator lights. No branching arrows or separate cables.
entries.why: Adds a wired networking object distinct from an antenna router.

entries.name: Server blade
entries.meaning: An individual computing module inside a server system.
entries.brief: One slim removable server blade with an integrated front handle, ventilation slots, and a small status light. No rack or arrows.
entries.why: A specific hardware noun that broadens the server vocabulary.

entries.name: Fiber optic connector
entries.meaning: A physical connection for high-speed data.
entries.brief: One fiber connector with a narrow ferrule, squared coupling body, ribbed strain relief, and a short attached cable end. No speed lines or arrows.
entries.why: Related fiber concepts exist; inspect them before commissioning this specific connector.

entries.name: Patch panel
entries.meaning: A fixed panel for organizing network connections.
entries.brief: One slim patch panel with two mounting ears and a single integrated row of ports. No cables, labels, or separate tools.
entries.why: Provides a passive networking component with a distinct silhouette.

entries.name: Sip and puff controller
entries.meaning: An assistive input device controlled through a mouth tube.
entries.brief: One compact controller with a single curved mouth tube attached to its small base and a simple integral mounting arm. Make the mouth tube and base read as one assembled device. Omit a person, wheelchair, computer, and airflow arrows.
entries.why: Adds a specific alternative-input subject. This is an exploratory device brief: check real device references and simplify the mounting structure before drawing.

entries.name: Flow meter
entries.meaning: A throughput metaphor based on a device that measures flow.
entries.brief: One compact inline flow meter: a central round dial body with two integral opposed pipe connections and a single needle. Include only a few ticks; omit numbers, fluid drops, arrows, and a surrounding pipe system.
entries.why: Exploratory metaphor for throughput. Its integral inlet and outlet should distinguish it from the existing Speedometer; reject the proposal if it only reads as another gauge.

entries.name: Bellows
entries.meaning: A compression metaphor based on a hand-operated air tool.
entries.brief: One pair of hand bellows in side view, with a pleated flexible chamber between two tapered boards, an integrated narrow nozzle, and attached handles. Omit emitted air, motion marks, fire, and a hand.
entries.why: Exploratory metaphor: the compressible chamber suggests reducing volume. A distinct object rather than a file with inward-pointing arrows; test whether the meaning is useful in context.

entries.name: Ink brayer
entries.meaning: An ink roller for applying a consistent layer; a styling metaphor.
entries.brief: One hand brayer with a broad cylindrical roller held in an attached U-shaped yoke and a short central handle. Show the complete tool at a slight diagonal. Omit an ink tray, paper, paint trail, and a hand.
entries.why: Exploratory metaphor for applying visual treatment. Different from a paintbrush: the single roller and yoke should establish its identity without a background surface.

entries.name: Bookbinding press
entries.meaning: A binding tool; a metaphor for assembling finished content.
entries.brief: One tabletop bookbinding press with two broad horizontal wooden plates joined by two upright threaded screws and integrated wing handles. Show the plates slightly separated. Omit a book, loose pages, letters, and a person.
entries.why: Exploratory editorial metaphor. Keep it visually distinct from the single-screw Printing press; if both collapse to the same silhouette at 48 pixels, choose only one.

entries.name: Microfilm reel
entries.meaning: A physical reel used to preserve and retrieve archived material.
entries.brief: One small microfilm reel viewed obliquely, with a solid circular flange, central spindle opening, and a short attached strip emerging from the wound film. Keep the strip blank and omit a projector, document, images, and separate reels.
entries.why: Adds a distinct archive medium. Existing voicemail reel symbols are related; inspect them before authoring and retain the physical reel-and-strip construction.

entries.name: Sextant
entries.meaning: A precision-navigation metaphor for finding a destination.
entries.brief: One sextant with a curved graduated arc, two joined radial arms, an integrated small telescope along the upper arm, and a compact handle. Use sparse ticks without numerals; omit a horizon, globe, star, or person.
entries.why: Exploratory discovery metaphor. The triangular arm-and-arc silhouette gives it a different visual identity from Compass; recognition should be checked before prioritizing it.

entries.name: Periscope
entries.meaning: A looking-beyond-the-surface metaphor for previews and inspection.
entries.brief: One standalone periscope instrument with a long upright tube, a short upper elbow with an integrated viewing opening, and a lower eyepiece bending in the opposite direction. Omit a submarine, waves, eye glyph, and viewer.
entries.why: Existing periscope references are embedded in submarines. Propose the complete instrument by itself, with its own eyepiece and upper viewing head; this is a metaphor rather than a standard preview symbol.

entries.name: Optical transceiver
entries.meaning: A removable module that connects equipment to an optical network.
entries.brief: One compact optical transceiver viewed at a slight angle: a narrow metal body, a pair of integrated optical sockets on its front, and a small bail latch. Omit a switch, cable, arrows, labels, and emitted light.
entries.why: Adds the network module itself, distinct from the existing Fiber optic connector proposal. Keep the module body, front sockets, and latch readable; simplify minor engineering details.

entries.name: Network cable tester
entries.meaning: A handheld instrument for checking network cables.
entries.brief: One compact handheld cable tester with a single integrated network socket at its top, a vertical row of small indicator apertures, and one recessed button. Omit readable labels, a separate remote unit, cable, checkmark, and fault symbols.
entries.why: Adds a diagnostic tool for maintaining website infrastructure. Recognition relies on the socket and indicator row; it should not become a generic phone or remote control.

entries.name: Powerline adapter
entries.meaning: A plug-in adapter that carries a network connection through power wiring.
entries.brief: One wall-plug powerline network adapter shown obliquely, with a compact upright body, integral mains prongs at the back, one Ethernet port on the lower edge, and a small indicator light. Omit a wall socket, lightning bolt, paired adapter, and cable.
entries.why: Adds a specific complete networking device. Differentiate it from a generic charger using the integral Ethernet port; do not add a separate network symbol.

entries.name: Wi-Fi range extender
entries.meaning: A device that extends wireless network coverage.
entries.brief: One compact plug-in wireless range extender with two short attached side antennae, integral rear mains prongs, and a central pairing button. Omit radio-wave glyphs, a router, coverage rings, arrows, and a wall.
entries.why: Adds a wall-plug networking form distinct from the desktop Router. Antennae and prongs are natural device parts; avoid a separate Wi-Fi signal overlay.

entries.name: Web globe
entries.meaning: The web as a globally connected place.
entries.brief: A freestanding globe with a few latitude and longitude lines. No browser, pointer, or surrounding orbit.
entries.why: Keep one recognizable globe; add web-related aliases.

entries.name: Compass
entries.meaning: Finding a destination or exploring content.
entries.brief: A circular compass with one integrated needle and minimal direction ticks. No map or location pin.
entries.why: A shared navigation object gives Websites a clear discovery concept.

entries.name: Anchor
entries.meaning: A stable destination within a page.
entries.brief: One nautical anchor with its ring, shank, curved arms, and flukes. No chain, page, or link badge.
entries.why: Use as a metaphor; the visual noun stays Anchor.

entries.name: Chain links
entries.meaning: A connection between web resources.
entries.brief: Two naturally interlocking chain links, treated as one piece of chain. No broken segment or status mark.
entries.why: Reuse across categories instead of drawing a category-specific link.

entries.name: Cookie
entries.meaning: Stored preferences and website tracking.
entries.brief: One round cookie with a few integrated chocolate chips and a simple bitten edge. No shield or checkmark.
entries.why: The food object already supplies the familiar web metaphor.

entries.name: Padlock
entries.meaning: Restricted access and secure content.
entries.brief: One closed padlock with an arched shackle and a plain body. No toggle, checkmark, or document.
entries.why: Replace lock-plus-toggle combinations with the reusable lock object.

entries.name: Fingerprint
entries.meaning: Biometric identity and authentication.
entries.brief: One fingertip ridge pattern, with open curved ridges forming a clear oval. No scanning frame or device.
entries.why: Inspect the original before reuse; isolate the fingerprint if needed.

entries.name: Spider
entries.meaning: An automated crawler that discovers pages.
entries.brief: One spider with a compact body and eight legs. No web, magnifying glass, or browser.
entries.why: Keep Spider as the name; Web crawler belongs in aliases.

entries.name: Server rack
entries.meaning: The hardware that hosts websites.
entries.brief: One upright server rack with integrated equipment bays and small indicator lights. No wings, motion lines, or cloud.
entries.why: Reuse plain server hardware; migration is a separate action.

entries.name: Database
entries.meaning: Structured information stored for a website.
entries.brief: One cylindrical database object with two or three integrated tiers. No arrows, document, or lock.
entries.why: Use one database across Websites, Programming, and Diagrams.

entries.name: Router
entries.meaning: A device that routes network traffic.
entries.brief: One low router body with two attached antennae and a few integrated port details. No floating Wi-Fi symbol.
entries.why: A hardware noun with clear cross-category reuse.

entries.name: Hourglass
entries.meaning: Time spent waiting for a page or process.
entries.brief: One upright hourglass with two bulbs, narrow waist, top and base, and an integrated sand mound. No arrow or clock badge.
entries.why: A reusable time object; timeout is an alias, not a new drawing.

entries.name: Speedometer
entries.meaning: The speed of a website or service.
entries.brief: One gauge with a curved dial, sparse ticks, and an integrated needle. No browser frame or lightning badge.
entries.why: The source called Performance metrics is a browser frame; a gauge conveys speed directly.

entries.name: Funnel
entries.meaning: Filtering content or narrowing a selection.
entries.brief: One funnel with a broad open mouth tapering to a narrow spout. No stacked conversion stages or people.
entries.why: Use the recognizable object to avoid drawing an entire filtering interface.

entries.name: Magnet
entries.meaning: Attracting visitors and interest.
entries.brief: One horseshoe magnet with two integrated contrasting pole tips. No money, people, or floating attraction lines.
entries.why: A secondary metaphor for growth, shared with Design.

accessories.title: Accessories
accessories.summary: Expand beyond hats, eyewear, and necklaces with standalone hair accessories, fastening pieces, watch accessories, and everyday carry items.
accessories.principle: Name the accessory itself; draw one complete, recognizable object.

entries.name: Hair claw
entries.meaning: A spring clip that gathers and holds hair.
entries.brief: One closed hair claw in side view, with two curved interlocking toothed jaws, an integrated hinge, and two short squeeze handles. Show a few broad teeth; omit hair and a wearer.
entries.why: Introduces a common hair-fastening object absent from the checked standalone names. The jaws and squeeze handles distinguish it from a comb.

entries.name: Scrunchie
entries.meaning: A fabric-covered elastic used to tie hair.
entries.brief: One soft ring-shaped scrunchie viewed from above, with a clear central opening and a few rounded fabric gathers around an irregular outer edge. Omit hair, a wrist, and decorative bows.
entries.why: Adds a soft textile hair fastener, distinct from rigid jewelry loops. The gathered outline must carry its identity without detailed texture.

entries.name: Bobby pin
entries.meaning: A narrow pin that holds small sections of hair.
entries.brief: One complete bobby pin at a diagonal, with a long straight arm, a second gently waved arm, and a rounded joined end. Keep the open tips separated and omit hair.
entries.why: A compact fastening object with a distinctive straight-versus-waved construction. Existing hairpin-turn matches describe road geometry, not this accessory.

entries.name: Barrette
entries.meaning: A clasp that secures hair beneath a decorative top.
entries.brief: One barrette in side three-quarter view, with an elongated gently arched top plate and its attached curved spring clasp visible underneath. Omit hair, flowers, and a separate pin.
entries.why: Adds the plate-and-clasp construction, distinct from the toothed Hair claw and narrow Bobby pin. Avoid a featureless flat bar.

entries.name: Headband
entries.meaning: A curved band worn to keep hair away from the face.
entries.brief: One freestanding padded headband viewed obliquely, forming a broad open horseshoe with a slightly thickened crown and tapered rounded ends. Show the band thickness; omit a head and headphones.
entries.why: Related references show people wearing headbands. This proposal depicts the complete band alone and must remain distinguishable from a headphone arch.

entries.name: Tie clip
entries.meaning: A spring clasp that holds a necktie against a shirt.
entries.brief: One tie clip in side three-quarter view, with a slim rectangular front bar and an attached curved spring jaw tucked behind it. Show a small gap between the front and rear jaw; omit the tie and shirt.
entries.why: Complements existing neckties and bow ties with the fastening piece itself. Use the side construction to distinguish it from a plain line.

entries.name: Bolo tie
entries.meaning: A cord necktie fastened with a sliding ornamental clasp.
entries.brief: One complete bolo tie with an oval integrated slide at the meeting point of a loose upper cord loop and two hanging cord ends finished with narrow metal tips. Keep all parts connected as one wearable accessory; omit a shirt.
entries.why: Adds a structurally distinct neckwear subject. The cord loop and sliding clasp differ from the existing fabric necktie and bow tie.

entries.name: Pocket watch
entries.meaning: A portable watch carried in a pocket.
entries.brief: One closed-face pocket watch with a round dial, sparse hour ticks, two integral hands, a top winding crown, and an attached suspension bow. Omit numerals, a chain, and a wrist strap.
entries.why: Broadens the existing wristwatch subjects with a distinct crown-and-bow silhouette. Do not add a separate chain just to imply pocket use.

entries.name: Money clip
entries.meaning: A folded metal clip that holds folded banknotes.
entries.brief: One broad folded money clip in three-quarter view, with a flat front plate, a tight U-shaped bend, and a shorter rear plate visible behind it. Leave the clip empty and omit banknotes and currency symbols.
entries.why: Adds a pocket-carry object distinct from the existing wallets and coin purses. Its broad folded plate separates it from the slender Tie clip.

entries.name: Purse hook
entries.meaning: A portable hook for suspending a handbag from a table edge.
entries.brief: One portable purse hook unfolded, with a small round tabletop pad connected by an integral neck to a broad J-shaped hanging hook below. Omit the table and bag.
entries.why: Adds a complete bag accessory with a distinctive pad-and-hook silhouette. Its function can be explained in aliases without drawing a scene.

entries.name: Lanyard
entries.meaning: A neck loop for carrying a small personal item.
entries.brief: One complete lanyard forming a long soft fabric loop with two sides joining into an integrated swivel clasp at the bottom. Omit an ID card, key, whistle, and lettering.
entries.why: A whistle with a lanyard exists, but no standalone neck lanyard was found in the checked names. Propose the complete strap and its own clasp, without any carried object.

entries.name: Retractable key reel
entries.meaning: A spring reel that keeps an attached item within reach.
entries.brief: One retractable key reel with a compact round housing, a short extended cord, and a single split ring attached at its end. Include a small integrated mounting clip at the housing edge; omit keys and badges.
entries.why: Adds a mechanically distinct carry accessory. Housing, cord, and ring form one assembled object, rather than a key plus a separate symbol.

entries.name: Hair stick
entries.meaning: A long pin used to secure an updo.
entries.brief: One hair stick at a diagonal, with a long smoothly tapered shaft, a rounded point, and a small integrated bulb-shaped end. Omit hair, dangling charms, and a second stick.
entries.why: Extends the hair vocabulary to an updo tool. This is a lower-priority recognition check: the integrated finial should prevent it from reading as a needle or chopstick.

entries.name: Collar pin
entries.meaning: A short bar that joins the points of a shirt collar.
entries.brief: One collar pin shown horizontally, with a short slender shaft and a small rounded terminal at each end; make one terminal slightly longer to show its fastening sleeve. Omit the collar, tie, and chain.
entries.why: Adds a specific formal fastening object. Its simple bar silhouette may be ambiguous at 48 pixels, so keep this behind the more recognizable Tie clip.

entries.name: Watch strap
entries.meaning: A replacement band for attaching a watch to the wrist.
entries.brief: One continuous replacement watch strap laid in a gentle curve, with an integrated buckle and keeper at one end and a tapered perforated tail at the other. Omit the watch head and extra detached band pieces.
entries.why: Proposes the wearable band itself rather than another watch face. Use a one-piece strap construction to keep the subject complete; compare related belt and wristband references before drawing.

entries.name: Bag strap
entries.meaning: A detachable shoulder strap for a bag.
entries.brief: One broad adjustable bag strap arranged in a shallow U curve, with one integrated sliding adjuster and an attached swivel hook at each end. Keep the strap continuous and omit the bag and shoulder.
entries.why: Adds a useful replaceable accessory beyond complete bags. The broad strap and two end hooks distinguish it from a Lanyard.

entries.name: Hand muff
entries.meaning: A padded sleeve that keeps both hands warm.
entries.brief: One cylindrical fabric hand muff viewed at a slight angle, with a broad soft body and two rounded open ends connected by the padded sleeve. Suggest thickness with one inner rim; omit hands, cords, and fur texture.
entries.why: Expands cold-weather accessories beyond the many beanies and mittens. Both sleeve openings are important so it does not read as a bag or cushion.

entries.name: Bag tassel
entries.meaning: A hanging fringe ornament for a bag.
entries.brief: One complete bag tassel with a small attached loop, a compact binding cap, and a short curtain of broad fringe strands below. Keep the fringe joined beneath the cap; omit the bag, key, and letter charms.
entries.why: Related graduation-cap tassels exist. Propose a complete tassel accessory alone, using a broad fringe silhouette rather than repeating a cap composition.

entries.name: Ring mandrel
entries.meaning: A tapered tool used to size and shape finger rings.
entries.brief: One ring mandrel at a diagonal, with a long smoothly tapered round shaft, a short integrated handle at the broad end, and three shallow circumferential guide marks. Omit numbers, rings, a hammer, and a hand.
entries.why: Adds a jewelry-fitting tool adjacent to the category’s rings and display busts. The tapered shaft is the defining feature; if it reads only as a cone, leave it for later.

entries.name: Sock garter
entries.meaning: A leg band with an attached clip that holds up a sock.
entries.brief: One complete sock garter with a broad adjustable loop, a short attached hanging strap, and an integrated clasp at the bottom. Show the loop open in an oval so the band and hanging clip remain distinct; omit a leg and sock.
entries.why: Adds a specific clothing fastener beyond the existing shoulder suspenders. Keep this as one assembled wearable band rather than a pair arranged around legs.
